r7-bypass-adversarial.title: Adversarial bypass construction (as-of leakage + append-only)
r7-bypass-adversarial.imperative: Actually construct scratch probes to try to bypass the as-of leakage check and the append-only guarantee (not just read the code). Confirm the WHERE-clause-structure assertion inspects real SQL TEXT (not just bound params); confirm a session-unfiltered query would fail the check; confirm a lazier append-only implementation (INSERT OR REPLACE, or a UNIQUE constraint missing model_version) would fail the append-only test. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r7-bypass-adversarial.finding: Constructed 5 independent bypass scripts (not reusing the implementer's own tests), all in scratchpad (bypass_append_only.py, bypass_as_of_leakage.py): (1) INSERT OR REPLACE instead of plain INSERT -> confirmed the duplicate-key test would fail to observe IntegrityError (real bypass would be caught, test correctly refuses to pass silently). (2) UNIQUE key missing model_version -> confirmed a legitimate NEW-version insert (the exact scenario in test_older_model_version_row_survives) is wrongly rejected, so the gate test would ERROR loudly on this lazier key, catching it. (3) The handoff's named negative control (session-unfiltered SELECT, Python-side post-filter) -> confirmed the real checker (_all_statements_session_scoped, imported live from the test module, not reimplemented) returns False, correctly rejecting it. (4) A SUBTLER attack the handoff didn't name: a WHERE clause carrying session_type IN (...) syntactically but with the IN-list hardcoded to ALL FOUR sessions regardless of the as_of bound -- the text-only regex alone cannot distinguish this from a correctly-bound clause (confirmed: regex scores it True). However confirmed the co-located ROW-CONTENT assertions in the real gate tests (len==1 for FP1, exact axis-value match, FP3-excludes-Q) independently catch this exact bug class (a hardcoded-all-sessions load_as_of returns 4 rows, failing len==1) -- so the test suite AS A WHOLE is sound via defense-in-depth (SQL-shape check + data-content check), even though the SQL-shape check alone has this narrow blind spot. (5) Confirmed via a fresh independent trace-callback capture (not the implementer's) that the real store.load_as_of('FP2') binds literal ('FP1','FP2') only, never FP3/Q. No bypass of the shipped test suite succeeded. See OBSERVATION in review result re: finding (4) -- non-blocking, since it's a weakness in one component of a two-layer check, not in the end-to-end guarantee the tests actually enforce.
